question: Which classical Sanskrit play was written by Kalidasa?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhijnana-Shakuntalam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalidasa**, one of the greatest classical Sanskrit playwrights and poets, wrote **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam**, considered a masterpiece of Sanskrit literature.
 
• **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam**, often translated as "The Recognition of Shakuntala," is a play that revolves around the love story of King Dushyanta and Shakuntala, a maiden of extraordinary beauty.
 
• The play is famous for its rich poetic descriptions, emotional depth, and intricate portrayal of human relationships.
 
• **Kalidasa** is also credited with other celebrated works such as **Raghuvamsha** and **Kumarasambhava**, but **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam** stands out as his most renowned play.
 
• The story of **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam** is based on an episode from the **Mahabharata**, specifically the tale of Shakuntala and King Dushyanta from the **Adi Parva**.
 
• The work has been widely translated into numerous languages and has had a profound influence on Indian and global literature. It was the first Sanskrit work to be translated into European languages in the 18th century, making Kalidasa internationally recognized.
 
• **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam** embodies the classical Sanskrit theatrical tradition, adhering to the rules of dramaturgy outlined in the **Natyashastra**.
 
• The correct answer is **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam**, as it is authored by Kalidasa and widely revered as one of the greatest contributions to Indian classical literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kalidasa’s Contribution to Literature:**

 
 
• **Kalidasa** is renowned for his sophisticated and elegant style of writing, blending nature, emotions, and divine imagery seamlessly.
 
• He is often regarded as the **Shakespeare of India** due to his unparalleled contributions to drama and poetry in ancient Sanskrit literature.
 
• His works, apart from **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam**, include **Meghaduta** (The Cloud Messenger), **Kumarasambhava** (The Birth of Kumara), and **Raghuvamsha** (The Lineage of Raghu).
 
 
 
• **About the Play Abhijnana-Shakuntalam:**
 
 
• The play is divided into **seven acts**, depicting the journey of love, separation, and eventual reunion between King Dushyanta and Shakuntala.
 
• The central theme revolves around the concept of **love, memory, and recognition**, with a strong emphasis on destiny and divine intervention.
 
• The title, "Abhijnana," refers to the ring of recognition that plays a pivotal role in reuniting the lovers after a period of separation caused by a curse.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Mudrarakshasa:** Written by **Vishakhadatta**, this historical play focuses on the political strategies of Chanakya and the establishment of Chandragupta Maurya’s rule. *Not authored by Kalidasa.*
 
• **Svapnavasavadattam:** Written by **Bhasa**, this play narrates the story of King Udayana and his queen Vasavadatta. *Not authored by Kalidasa.*
 
• **Mrichchhakatika:** Also known as "The Little Clay Cart," this play was authored by **Shudraka** and deals with themes of love, morality, and social issues. *Not authored by Kalidasa.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Influence of Abhijnana-Shakuntalam:**

 
 
• **International Acclaim:** It was one of the first Sanskrit plays to be translated into European languages, introducing Indian literature to the Western world.
 
• **Translation:** The German translation by **Sir William Jones** in 1789 greatly popularized the play in Europe.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** The story of Shakuntala is deeply embedded in Indian culture, inspiring numerous art forms, including paintings, music, and dance.
